creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The reload path is exactly what the README promises - a file that will not parse changes nothing at all, and the log says so with an impact line and a check line (crates/muster-seam/src/handler.rs:985). What it does not do is reach the person who just saved the file.

They are in an editor, not in the run log. From the window's side a rejected save and a save that changed nothing look identical: nothing happens. The one moment somebody most needs telling is the moment they have just broken their config, and that is the moment Muster is quietest.

Left for a call rather than built, because every answer costs something the project has an opinion about. A banner over the window is chrome Muster otherwise does not have. A pane-sized notice is a pane nobody asked for. The title bar already carries daemon health and would then carry two unrelated things. Reusing the notification path is closest to what exists - attention routing is built, and this is arguably attention - but it stretches 'an agent needs you' to cover 'your file is broken'.

Worth an answer before anybody but the author edits a config file.
title: 🔇 A refused config reload is only ever a log line
